sources.title: Roger S. Bagnall and Peter Derow: The Hellenistic Period, documents 1, 6 and 8
sources.note: Direct publisher PDF read. Printed p.1/PDF index0: Alexander’s general and Phrygian appointment333; pp.8-10/index7-9:311 treaty and Skepsis decree; pp.16-18/index15-17:302 league and Ipsus ending. No blanket claim that command of Asia meant occupation of all Asia. Teos public paraphrases use the separately checked Welles translation below.

sources.title: Jona Lendering: Antigonus Monophthalmus
sources.note: Direct historical chronology read: 333 Phrygian satrapy; 323 Alexander’s death and retained territories; 320 supreme Asian command; 306 royal title; 301 Ipsus death and division. Bibliography includes Billows, Briant and Heckel. Used for broad chronology rather than disputed campaign-year details.

sources.title: Plutarch: Life of Demetrius, translated by Bernadotte Perrin
sources.note: Direct University of Chicago-hosted Loeb text read, chapters17-18 royal titles,28-30 Ipsus,37 Macedonia,52-53 death and dynastic continuation. Later ancient literary account, not an eyewitness to301 BCE. Modern editorial notes give306,301 and283 dates.

sources.title: Diodorus Siculus: Antigonus’s siege of Tyre, Library of History 19.58
sources.note: Direct translated primary account read:19.58.1-5 shipbuilding workers, Lebanon timber and shipyards. Later historian; no workforce figures treated as excavated counts. Intro315 date has scholarly variation315/314, so public wording mid310s BCE avoids artificial precision.

sources.title: C. Bradford Welles: First letter of Antigonus to Teos, Royal Correspondence 3
sources.note: Direct primary inscription translation read, sectionsB,C,H,J. Project dated broadly306-302 BCE, often c.303. Housing, burials, copied laws and grain fund were royal directions for a planned synoecism; implementation not assumed. Later study differs on how far project proceeded. Combined same-inscription budget includes PHI Greek text; no source splitting to increase allowance.

sources.title: Packard Humanities Institute Greek Inscriptions: Teos 59, letters of Antigonus I
sources.note: Direct scholarly Greek edition read, heading c.303 and inscription line6: τοῖς Λεβεδίοις ἀμισθί appears without restoration brackets. Translation cross-checked against Welles RC3 sectionB. The preceding initial letter of houses is restored, so omitted from specimen. Modern accents/type, not facsimile. Same original inscription as letter source, combined budget checked.

sources.title: University of Bonn: Priene, living in a Hellenistic city
sources.note: Direct archaeological project page read. Mid-fourth-century foundation, rooms around courtyard, initial diversity and changing plots; Lampon house modern study. Later destruction around140/130 BCE explicitly distinguished from Antigonus. No claim uniform plots prove equal wealth.

sources.title: Republic of Türkiye: Archaeological Site of Priene, UNESCO Tentative List submission
sources.note: Direct state submission read, Description paragraph on fourth-century town plan and springs/clay pipes/street drainage. General late-Classical/Hellenistic urban system, not an Antigonus-funded project. UNESCO tentative submission is not an accepted World Heritage designation or a peer-reviewed excavation report. Later gymnasium, baths and healing temple not assigned to Antigonus.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Silver tetradrachm of Demetrios Poliorketes, 05.44.399
sources.note: Direct collection page read:300-294 BCE coin, Salamis mint, Nike with trumpet on prow and Poseidon/trident, commemoration of306 victory. Public wording dates the surviving object after Antigonus’s death. No image-origin claim or excavated provenance.

proposedOverrides.name: Kingdom of Antigonus I
proposedOverrides.summary: Antigonus I’s Asian successor realm; the imported dates begin after his death at Ipsus in 301 BCE.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact missing indexed ID, separate narrative. No aliases.
batchIdentityNotes.historicalSpan: Power after Alexander’s death323 BCE; royal title306; death and division301. Demetrius continuation301-283 is explicitly separate.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded world-bc300 MultiPolygon bbox21.2204E30.4319N42.4390E40.5032N, eastern Mediterranean/Anatolia/Syrian region, not mainly later Macedonia. Public identification is a best-fit interpretation of name and outline; century-long survival rejected. No polygon correction or precise occupied-frontier certification.
batchIdentityNotes.related: Existing macedon-and-hellenic-league concerns the much later Doson/PhilipV/Perseus phase around224-168 BCE. Kingdom-of-Lysimachus is a rival successor state, not an alias. Alexander’s empire, Ptolemaic kingdom and modern macedonia remain separate.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Teos-Lebedos letters are planned measures, not proof of completed merger. Priene houses/infrastructure are regional context with their longer chronology explicit;140/130 destruction and300-294 coin are later. No universal sanitation, schooling or medical practice inferred. Religious imagery treated as beliefs and representation.
